subject: Some comments on Stan usage, emacs, and code management

messages.author: b6fd2925353976cd
messages.subject: Some comments on Stan usage, emacs, and code management
parts:
Thanks to everyone who responded to the lmer vs Stan comparison. I wanted to briefly respond to a few things that were said there:

Bob wrote: "Andrew's been using lmer and bglmer for years because he couldn't fit the models he wanted to in BUGS/JAGS."

But then I don't understand why Andrew always keeps saying use Stan whenever I ask him a question!!! :)

Bob wrote:  "I'll grin and bear the lack of indentation, but 
I would very very strongly recommend pulling the model 
out of the R code and into its own file.   I really don't like 
this tendency to bundle the model and code together that 
our examples in R are leading people to.  There's an emacs 
mode for Stan, for one thing! "

I developed RSI using emacs back in 2002 and had to quit using it. I am tied to RStudio for that reason, and I think there are others out there whose hands were ruined by emacs (I should have remapped the keys, but it's too late now).

Regarding bundling: Andrew told me that he does not release his code associated with his published work because he has lots of different files and he doesn't have time to put them together to release his code. (This is astonishing because he goes after people for not releasing their data/code!!!! See: http://www.stat.columbia.edu/~gelman/research/published/ChanceEthics1.pdf, and see http://andrewgelman.com/wp-content/uploads/2012/03/chanceletters.pdf)

In order to help Andrew meet the standards he advocates for open data and open methods, it would help him to have a simple workflow that can actually result in a code+data release upon publication. A single file to work with will probably do the job (it will be messy, but it's better than nothing). In Gelman and Hill 2007, it was a real headache to figure out how the radon data got assembled ready for analysis. It needed some detective work and quite a bit of code rewriting. 

There are lots of people out there like Andrew who would benefit from a single file world view, because then they can actually release their code.

best,

--
Shravan Vasishth
Professor für Psycholinguistik und Neurolinguistik
Department Linguistik
Universität Potsdam, D-14476 Potsdam
http://www.ling.uni-potsdam.de/~vasishth
